decisions.target: Passengers booked on Kestrel flights to or from Orlando or Philadelphia between December 21 and December 27

actions.action: Free changes and cancellations for bookings in a 2-week window

decisions.message: Kestrel Air update: workers at our ground handling contractor in Orlando and Philadelphia plan a 48-hour strike on Dec 22-23, so some flights may be late or canceled. If you are booked between Dec 14 and Dec 27, you can change or cancel for free in the app now: Dec 21 and Dec 24 still have seats. If your flight is canceled, we will rebook you on the next Kestrel flight with a free seat or refund you in full.
decisions.why:
With no action, 9% of customers leave and only 89-92% of week 5-10 revenue is kept.
Free changes in week 7 move 6-9 of 36 customers off Dec 22-23 and keep 94-98% of revenue (+$7-11M).
It costs only $0.2M, cuts switching from 9% to 3-6%, and saves our second action for the next surprise.

decisions.target: Passengers whose Kestrel flight was canceled or delayed more than 3 hours between December 21 and December 27

actions.action: Goodwill for affected passengers, up to 10,000 passengers
Extra airport and call-center staff for 2 weeks
Double loyalty points for affected passengers

decisions.message: Kestrel Air: we are sorry the Dec 22-23 strike disrupted your holiday trip. We have added a $75 Kestrel travel credit and double Kestrel Club points for that trip to your account. Extra staff are at our Orlando and Philadelphia airports and on our phone lines through January 10. If you are owed a refund, it is being paid automatically to your original payment method.
decisions.why:
Complaints and NPS are judged against last winter, and the disrupted passengers are where both are made or lost.
A travel credit costs less than cash and is mostly used on seats that would fly empty.
Extra staff shorten the wait when people call back after the holidays.
